theme: The ascension; choosing Matthias, preparing for power
readingInstruction: Read Acts 1:1-26. Luke picks up where his Gospel ended: Jesus appears alive for forty days, promises the Spirit, and ascends. The disciples wait and pray, and a twelfth apostle is chosen. Notice the commission in verse 8, which is also the outline of the whole book.
settingTheScene: Acts is the second volume of Luke’s work, addressed again to Theophilus. If the Gospel tells all that Jesus began to do and teach, Acts tells what he continued to do by his Spirit through his church. It covers about thirty years, from the ascension around AD 30 to Paul’s imprisonment in Rome around AD 60. Its title, “Acts of the Apostles,” is a little misleading. The main actor is the risen Lord, working by the Holy Spirit.
observation: “He presented himself alive to them after his suffering by many proofs, appearing to them during forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God” (1:3).
“For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now” (1:5).
“Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” (1:6).
“But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth” (1:8).
“He was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight” (1:9).
“This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven” (1:11).
“All these with one accord were devoting themselves to prayer” (1:14).
“You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two you have chosen” (1:24).
interpretation:
Luke says that Jesus showed himself alive by “many proofs.” The resurrection was not a vision or a feeling. It was a public fact, and the disciples were eyewitnesses. For forty days he taught them about the kingdom of God. Then he told them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father, the baptism with the Holy Spirit.

The disciples ask, “Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” They are still thinking in terms of a political restoration. Jesus does not rebuke the question, but redirects it. The times are the Father’s business. Their business is to be witnesses, and the power to do it will come from the Spirit. Then comes the outline of Acts: Jerusalem (chapters 1 to 7), Judea and Samaria (8 to 12), and the end of the earth (13 to 28). The gospel will move outward in widening circles.

Then he is lifted up, and a cloud receives him. Two men in white say, “Why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus will come in the same way as you saw him go.” The ascension is not an absence. He is enthroned, and he will return. The disciples go back to Jerusalem filled with joy (Luke 24:52), and gather in the upper room with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers. They devote themselves to prayer. This is how a church waits: together, in prayer.

Peter then leads the group to replace Judas. The qualification is that the replacement must have been with them from the baptism of John to the ascension and must be a witness to the resurrection. They propose two men, pray, and cast lots, and the lot falls on Matthias. Christians have differed on whether this was the right choice, since Paul is later called an apostle. But the point is that the Twelve, representing the twelve tribes of renewed Israel, are restored to their number before Pentecost.
connection: Luke 24:47-53 is the end of Luke’s Gospel, with the same promise and ascension. Joel 2:28-29 promised the Spirit. Ezekiel 36:26-27 and Jeremiah 31:33 promised a new heart and the Spirit within. Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13 are the background to the ascension and the cloud. Isaiah 49:6 is the light to the ends of the earth. Psalm 69:25 and 109:8 are cited for Judas’s replacement. Matthew 28:18-20 is the Great Commission.
application:
Memorize Acts 1:8 this week. It is the memory verse of the unit.

Wait before you act. Spend time in prayer, with others if you can, before an important decision.

Think about your own Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and ends of the earth. Who is in each circle for you?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for showing himself alive by many proofs.
Thank him for the promise of the Spirit.
Ask him to make you a witness where you are.
